1.Name: Liquidity quotes passively, retains FIFO and cannot reverse through an exit
1.Detail: Entries do not pay the spread; existing quotes keep priority; inventory exits are reduce-only

2.Name: Liquidity pauses before depletion and waits for real exit liquidity
2.Detail: Underfunded bots reduce to flat and stay paused; only explicit restored equity permits new risk

3.Name: Paused liquidity preserves a triggered protective exit and its priority
3.Detail: Pausing cancels entry risk without cancelling or reprioritizing a pending protective exit

4.Name: Legacy liquidity inventory receives stops without widening existing protection
4.Detail: Legacy positions gain bounded protection on a decision; tighter stops survive

5.Name: Bot scale-ins and partial fills never loosen stops in either direction
5.Detail: Long and short averaging-down preserves the original stop

6.Name: Makers withdraw stale value risk before minimum rest and never take liquidity
6.Detail: Materially stale quotes cancel immediately; replacements remain passive

7.Name: Public time-weighted signal cannot see hidden fair value
7.Detail: Duration weighting is exact; hidden generator changes cannot change reversal decisions

8.Name: V19 upgrade preserves economic state and current format resumes deterministically
8.Detail: No funding or trades at migration; exact replay retains quotes, stops, signal history and RNG

9.Name: Earlier liquidity policies acquire new sizing settings without funding; version bump leaves fresh trading identical
9.Detail: V1 acquires V2 fields with no balance change; version-only changes produce identical trades and RNG

1.Name: Protective public midpoint tracks up and down without stale-price bias
1.Detail: A stale belief or hidden fair value cannot manufacture an entry when price equals the public midpoint

2.Name: Reversion needs observed-price distance and an actual turn in both directions
2.Detail: Continuations blocked; observed-price turns admitted independently of private fair value

3.Name: Unconfirmed Reversion reductions cannot reverse or exceed the remaining position
3.Detail: Warmup and confirmation do not block reductions; five requested contracts are capped to one

4.Name: Time windows are independent of trade count, bounded, and require fresh history
4.Detail: One sample per second; at most 62 samples; execution bursts cannot shorten the horizon

5.Name: Scalpers admit affordable small moves but reject flat prices and poor targets
5.Detail: A genuine two-tick move can trade; flat tape and inadequate target room cannot

6.Name: V17 strategy migration preserves ledgers and orders; current format resumes exactly
6.Detail: No deposits, withdrawals, trades or account/order changes on upgrade; exact resumed signals and RNG

1.Name: Every trading profile and decision is independent of hidden value and future news
1.Detail: Seven trader types initialize, observe and submit identically with opposite hidden values and future schedules

2.Name: Trader paths cannot read private market fields even with a legacy profile
2.Detail: Private generator fields are guarded during adoption and every strategy path

3.Name: Public quote matches the player snapshot and falls back safely without a two-sided book
3.Detail: The strategy and client share executable bid/ask filtering; empty sides use last trade

4.Name: Adoption cancels private entries and parent intent while preserving inventory and exits
4.Detail: Idempotent adoption retains cash, positions, stops and reduce-only exits without fills or random draws

5.Name: Makers and reserves retain private valuation and are excluded from adoption
5.Detail: Both infrastructure groups continue repricing from internal fair value

6.Name: V20 adoption preserves economics and V21 checkpoints replay exactly
6.Detail: Restore itself preserves state; first-step adoption is saved and exact continuation survives encode/decode

1.Name: Larger real quotes fill a 143-contract market order in both directions

2.Name: Consumed quotes replenish after a short delay; partial quotes retain priority
2.Detail: 1.5-second refill delay; existing partial quote preserved

3.Name: Larger quotes fit available inventory and capital without resetting balances
3.Detail: Quotes capped at five per side; no quotes with zero buying power

4.Name: Thin liquidity regimes retain smaller finite depth
4.Detail: Stress still reduces size and depth

5.Name: Old worlds adopt tuning without altering accounts, tape or resting orders during restore
5.Detail: Restore preserves history and accounts; makers adopt the policy on their next turn; replay remains exact

1.Name: Stats reconcile type/market totals, include retiring bots and exclude private accounts

2.Name: Inspection and formatting are deterministic and do not mutate the exchange

3.Name: Reports use refresh P&L baselines instead of counting historical profit or funding

4.Name: Depleted equity, pending exits, working and queued orders are counted accurately

5.Name: Empty populations format without division by zero

6.Name: Exact stats parsing and server ownership prevent unauthorized report generation

7.Name: Group-owner reports are private and unavailable worlds fail closed
